title: Project Overview
description: VoxelBlade is a web-based damage calculator and build optimizer for the Roblox game 'Voxel Blade'. It simulates weapon stats, enchantments, perks, and other game mechanics to calculate damage output and compare different builds. This Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite application is a single-page app served from index.html and mounted via src/main.ts. The README documents the recommended IDE setup (VS Code + Svelte extension), why plain Vite was chosen over SvelteKit, and TypeScript configuration decisions.

title: Core Type Definitions
description: Every module in the codebase imports from src/lib/types.ts — it is the most depended-upon file (12 importers) and defines the shared vocabulary: BuildState, equipment stats, perk interfaces, enchantment slots, damage type maps, and all game data structures. Understanding these types is essential before exploring any other layer, as they form the contract between the UI, engine, and data layers.

title: Shared Utilities and Constants
description: Two foundational modules sit beneath nearly everything else. src/lib/utils.ts (11 importers) provides rounding helpers, proc chance calculation, warding debuff math, and text highlighting. The src/lib/constants barrel re-exports over a dozen sub-modules — game-wide values (level caps, HP formulas, CDR values, damage type metadata, boost multipliers, and thresholds). Together they supply the numeric foundation for every calculation in the engine.
languageLesson: TypeScript barrel files (index.ts re-exporting sub-modules) let consumers import from a single path (e.g. '@lib/constants') while keeping each constant domain in its own file for maintainability.

title: Game Data Definitions
description: The src/data directory contains both TypeScript modules and JSON schema files defining every game entity: 11 races, guilds with rank progressions, 100+ armors, blades, handles, essences, gloves, rings, runes, enchantments, and the massive perks.json (3,688 lines) that the entire damage engine references. These static datasets are loaded at build time and drive every calculation path in the application.
languageLesson: JSON schema files in src/data/ serve as structured game data. They are not validated at runtime — instead, TypeScript types from types.ts define the expected shape, and Vite's static asset importing provides the data at build time.

title: Engine Core — Build Calculation
description: The engine orchestrator lives at src/lib/engine/build.ts — the file with the highest fan-out (16 dependencies). Its calcBuild function accumulates stats and perks from every equipment slot (race, guild, armor, ring, rune, weapon), applies enchantments and infusions, finalizes perks with effectiveness scaling, computes CDR, boosts, crit, and assembles active buffs. It imports from weapon.ts, enchant.ts, shrine.ts, data.ts, and dozens of data modules. This is the heart of the damage calculator.

title: Weapon and Enchantment Engines
description: Weapon calculation (src/lib/engine/weapon.ts) combines blade/handle stats, scalings, damage types, and perks — detecting hybrid bonuses and applying shrine multipliers. Monk weapons follow a separate path via calcMonkWeapon. The enchantment engine (src/lib/engine/enchant.ts) applies stat-selecting enchants (Restored/Flawless), direct modifiers, perk effectiveness scaling, and infusion's 50% stat halving. Both modules depend on the data barrel (engine/data.ts) for game entity lookups.

title: Critical Hits, Defense, and Damage Types
description: Three engine modules handle specific damage sub-systems. src/lib/crit.ts calculates crit chance and damage with perk-specific formulas (Flowing Crits, Sharp Crits, Thief Training, etc.). src/lib/defense.ts resolves armor defense breakdowns across damage types using the DEF_GROUP mapping. src/lib/damageTypeResolve.ts converts weapon art damage type strings into numeric maps, applying Fire↔Air conversion (Echo Incineration) and Air→Magic conversion (Spirit Winds). Together they complete the damage formula pipeline.
languageLesson: The defense module exports a DEF_GROUP constant that maps each of the 11 damage types to its applicable defense stat — this pattern of mapping enums to subsets is common in game engines to avoid switch/case explosion.

title: Buff and Boost Systems
description: The buff system (src/data/BuffData.ts) assembles all active buffs from perks, weapon arts, and runes, calculating potency and duration with stacking rules. The boost system (src/data/Boost.ts) defines 30+ damage boosts (Blood Thirsty, Frenzy, Primal, Penance, Vampire) each with custom calcFn closures. TypedDmgBoost.ts aggregates per-damage-type multipliers from these boosts. These modules form the post-calculation damage amplification layer that sits on top of the raw engine output.
languageLesson: Boost definitions use a factory pattern with calcFn closures — each boost captures its own calculation logic, allowing the boost system to handle both simple multiplier-per-perk values and complex conditional formulas without external branching.

title: State Management with Svelte Stores
description: src/lib/store.ts is the central state management layer (11 outgoing edges). It exports reactive Svelte stores for the entire build configuration and provides updater functions: loadBuild (localStorage deserialization with defaults fallback), setEnchantment (delegates to engine's enforceEnchantSlot), swapEnchantments, moveArmorSlot/moveRingSlot (clone-or-swap between primary and infusion slots), and setGuild (with race auto-override for Draconic). The store imports from the engine to validate enchantment constraints at write time.

title: Main Application Component
description: src/App.svelte is the root UI orchestrator (fan-out: 10). It composes the DamageAnalyzer, BuffList, LevelBar, EmotionalTracker, CdrStepsCalc, DraconicAbilityStats, and AppHeader — wiring each to the reactive store. It manages the Overview/Analyze tab switching and the overall layout. The component sits at the top of the import tree and is mounted by src/main.ts into the div#app element defined in index.html.

title: Damage Display and Analysis UI
description: The damage display layer consists of BaseDamageCalc (raw damage values from weapon stats), DamageAnalyzer (full breakdown by type with defense calculations), DmgTotalTooltip (pie chart of damage type distribution), and BuffList (active buff/debuff display). These components read computed values from the engine and render them with the project's custom UI components (Card, Badge, Stat, Panel from src/lib/ui/). The EmotionalTracker and CdrStepsCalc add interactive controls for situational modifiers.
languageLesson: Svelte 5's $props() rune replaces the traditional props declaration. Components like Stat.svelte use $props() to destructure named props, enabling TypeScript inference for component interfaces without explicit prop type declarations.

title: Modal System and Equipment Selection
description: The modal system provides the build configuration interface. RaceModal, GuildModal, WeaponPartModal, and AccessorySelectModal each wrap their content in the reusable Modal component (with backdrop, focus trapping, and fly-in animation). ModalSearchHeader provides shared search, tag filtering, stat filtering, and suggestion dropdowns. BuildSaves (~1,100 lines) handles localStorage-based save slots with drag-to-reorder, export/import (compressed base64), and fuzzy search. This is where users configure their builds.

title: Project Configuration and Deployment
description: The project root contains the full build and deployment configuration. package.json defines the ESM project with Svelte 5, Vite 8, Vitest, and PWA support. The GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/static.yml) builds the project and deploys to GitHub Pages. Vercel is also configured for hosting. TypeScript configuration is split across tsconfig.json (IDE default), tsconfig.app.json (application source targeting ES2023), and tsconfig.node.json (build tooling). Fallow provides dead-code analysis and security scanning.
languageLesson: VitePWA (configured in vite.config.ts) enables offline support via a service worker with StaleWhileRevalidate caching. The VITE_BASE_PATH env var allows the same build to deploy to different base paths (GitHub Pages subdirectory vs. Vercel root).
